plan.understanding: Round over the sharp perimeter of the scroll-wheel opening by adding a 2.0 mm fillet so the slot edges feel smooth.

subtasks.goal:
Apply a 2.0 mm constant-radius round to the scroll-wheel slot opening rim on the main housing (solid #0) by targeting the slot’s edge loop as the *inner boundary* of the exterior/top planar face whose normal points approximately in −Z (planar face with n≈[-0.024, 0, -1], area≈59.212, center≈[27.956, 15.571, 59.222]).

Method (in order):
1) Work on solid #0 only; explicitly exclude solid #1 (the separate scroll-wheel body) from selection/feature scope.
2) Select the exterior/top planar face on solid #0 with n≈[-0.024, 0, -1] and extract its boundary wires; identify the *inner* wire located nearest the scroll-wheel body’s centroid (solid #1 center≈[27.881, 22.101, 51.256]) and within/adjacent to the scroll-wheel body’s bbox region (x≈25.423..30.420, y≈15.069..29.133, z≈44.238..58.299). This inner wire is the slot opening rim.
3) Apply a 2.0 mm constant-radius fillet to the complete edge loop of that inner wire (all edge types in the loop), producing a smooth rim around the slot opening on the housing.
4) If an edge-blend/fillet feature cannot be solved on that loop, replace the rim explicitly: offset the top face and the slot-wall faces adjacent to the inner wire by 2.0 mm, build the blend surface from the offset-face intersection/rolling-ball equivalent, trim away the sharp corner, sew the new blend faces into the housing, and re-solidify—still affecting only solid #0.

Verification target: the geometric change must occur on the housing around the slot opening rim; solid #1 must remain unchanged (0 change to its volume/geometry).
